/MONDAY THROUGH SATURDAY/...
Issued at 257 AM EDT Sun Jul 26 2026

Monday - Tuesday Night...

Complicated early week forecast with multiple hazards possible, in 
addition to a temperature forecast that will be dependent on 
convective activity. We'll be situated in a NW flow aloft pattern on 
the eastern periphery of a strong western/central CONUS ridge 
through early week. This will put us in a strongly unstable airmass 
(SB CAPE over 3000 J/KG), and also in the presence of seasonably 
strong mid and upper level wind fields thanks to a persistent exit 
region of an upper level jet nosing into the Ohio River Valley. It 
is possible that a convective complex could be ongoing across the 
area on Monday morning, although confidence is lower than normal at 
this range as model data (including CAMs) have been inconsistent 
with this scenario. For now, let's assume a dry start to the day.

The first concern for Monday will be temperatures warming into the 
lower 90s in addition to dew points climbing well into the 70s for 
most, especially along and west of I-65. This would yield max heat 
indices in the 105-110F range along and west of I-65, and in the 
upper 90s and low 100s across our eastern third or so of the CWA. A 
Heat Advisory for half to two-thirds of our western CWA is likely in 
this scenario, although it comes with a caveat. The potential for 
the morning MCS and its convectively reinforced cold pool wrecking 
the temperature forecast, and/or an afternoon MCS diving into our 
area from upstream. As a result, won't be too quick to lift a 
headline until we are more confident in the convective evolution of 
upstream MCS potential. The same type of scenario also applies for 
Tuesday with similar values both in the T/Td department, maybe 
slightly less. So, we'll take a "wait and see" approach but will 
also continue to message the conditional heat/humidity threat to 
partners.

Back to the severe threats for Monday/Tuesday. Regardless of whether 
we get a Monday AM MCS, we do expect to become strongly unstable 
again by later Monday afternoon and evening. Forecast models 
continue to suggest upstream MCS activity gets going, and then has a 
good chance of diving into our area. The combination of 700-300 mb 
mean wind fields combined with any notable instability gradients are 
usually pretty good at steering these cold pool driven / forward 
propagating MCS's. As a result, do think we'll see impacts from at 
least 1, if not multiple thunderstorm complexes Monday and Tuesday. 
Given the amount of instability, deep layer shear (especially mid to 
upper level speed shear), and the likelihood of additional help from 
a developed cold pool from upstream activity think the main concern 
will be damaging winds. Perhaps a widespread damaging wind threat 
could develop if things really get going. Most likely locations for 
this would be across our NE CWA. Prolific lighting, and some 
potential for localized heavy rainfall may also develop. These 
systems usually tend to be progressive, however will have to watch 
for some training potential where the western flank of any MCS gets 
left behind by the surging cold pool. Will still be tons of 
instability in these areas, but will be oriented more parallel to 
the mean deep layer flow and could overachieve on rainfall. Right 
now, the most consistent signal for an impactful MCS would be later 
Monday evening into Monday night. Like the idea of SPC messaging the 
severe risk, albeit it is still conditional upon storm track.

Wednesday - Friday...

The mid to late week time frame looks fairly quiet as we remain in 
NW flow aloft, but this flow will be rather unremarkable with 
respect to any triggering shortwave features. In addition, surface 
high pressure builds in behind the departing cool front associated 
with the late Monday/early Tuesday system passing through the Great 
Lakes. The end result should be a mostly dry forecast with 
temperatures settling back around normal for this time of year in 
the upper 80s.

Saturday...

Quite a bit of uncertainty by early next weekend. It appears a 
stronger shortwave may round the top of the upper ridge and try to 
dig into the mid Mississippi River Valley. This could be a trigger 
for scattered showers and storms by Saturday. Quite a bit of complex 
upper pattern evolution before we get to that point, so will keep 
this low confidence for now. Temps should generally be around normal 
for this time of year, still in the upper 80s.
